storeMix.title: Store network: self-operated vs distributor
storeMix.content:
Self-operated stores are run and staffed directly by EEKA; distributor stores are run by independent third parties under EEKA's brands.

For EEKA Fashion Holdings Limited (贏家時尚控股有限公司): the self-operated count has fallen every period since its FY2021 peak of 1,558 to 1,276 at H1 FY2026 -- roughly 18% of the self-operated fleet closed in under five years. Distributor count has been comparatively stable (440 FY2019 to 397 H1 FY2026), so the mix shift is a self-operated retreat, not a franchising strategy.

What to watch:

  • Whether store closures are being offset by higher sales per remaining store, or are a straight scale-down
  • Distributor count holding up while self-operated shrinks -- a sign of channel substitution rather than total-market retreat
  • Total store count (right axis) against Revenue: fewer stores with flat or growing revenue implies online and per-store productivity are doing the work

channelRevenue.title: Online vs wholesale revenue
channelRevenue.content:
Online sales is e-commerce revenue; wholesale revenue is sales to distributors who then sell on through their own stores. Neither includes self-operated retail, which is the largest channel and is reported separately as SegmentRevenueRetail.

For EEKA Fashion Holdings Limited (贏家時尚控股有限公司): online sales have grown from RMB893m (FY2022) to RMB1,265m (FY2025) even as the self-operated store count fell, making e-commerce the channel absorbing demand that bricks-and-mortar retail is shedding. Wholesale revenue is smaller and more volatile (RMB334m FY2022 down to RMB201m FY2025), consistent with the flat-to-declining distributor store count.

What to watch:

  • Online sales growth rate against the self-operated store decline -- is e-commerce fully offsetting the lost physical footprint
  • Wholesale revenue per distributor store, since the store count alone is stable but revenue is not
  • Online gross margin, typically lower than self-operated retail on discounting and platform fees (not separately disclosed here)

inventoryDays.title: Inventory days
inventoryDays.content:
Inventory days (days inventory outstanding) is average inventory divided by cost of revenue, times the days in the period -- how long stock sits before it is sold. Apparel inventory also carries season risk: unsold stock ages into markdown territory.

For EEKA Fashion Holdings Limited (贏家時尚控股有限公司): inventory days rose from 320 (FY2024) to 386 (FY2025), a two-month-plus increase that lines up with the self-operated store closures and softer wholesale sell-through -- stock is moving more slowly through a shrinking store network. Only FY2024 and FY2025 are disclosed, so there is no pre-decline baseline to compare against.

What to watch:

  • Further increases, which would point to markdown risk and gross-margin pressure ahead
  • Inventory days against the store-mix chart: a shrinking self-operated fleet should need less working capital, not more, if sell-through holds
  • Discontinuation disclosed only annually, so interim swings are invisible between FY prints

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For EEKA Fashion Holdings Limited (贏家時尚控股有限公司): equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For EEKA Fashion Holdings Limited (贏家時尚控股有限公司): the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For EEKA Fashion Holdings Limited (贏家時尚控股有限公司): read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For EEKA Fashion Holdings Limited (贏家時尚控股有限公司): the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For EEKA Fashion Holdings Limited (贏家時尚控股有限公司): the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For EEKA Fashion Holdings Limited (贏家時尚控股有限公司): the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For EEKA Fashion Holdings Limited (贏家時尚控股有限公司): CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For EEKA Fashion Holdings Limited (贏家時尚控股有限公司): the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For EEKA Fashion Holdings Limited (贏家時尚控股有限公司): the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For EEKA Fashion Holdings Limited (贏家時尚控股有限公司): the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
